purpose: Truthful row-level audit of every currently pending DOC/DOCX feature-matrix row against the finalized native Word corpus. This file supplements coverage.json and does not change fixture_status or common metadata.

scope.classification_rule: Each pending row receives exactly one bounded category; native_fixture_evidence_available means only the cited native subset was observed, never that the broad matrix row is complete.

native_evidence_catalog.scope: Native Word DOC and DOCX with paragraphs, styles, numbering, fields, bookmarks and hyperlinks.
Native Word DOC, DOCX and RTF with tables, nested/merged cells, sections, page layout and note placement.
Native Word DOC, DOCX and RTF with revisions, comments, bookmarks, fields and review stories.
Native Word DOC, DOCX, DOTX and RTF with OMML/legacy equation, TOC/navigation, fields, numbering and bibliography custom XML.
Native Word DOC, DOCX and RTF with OfficeArt/VML/DrawingML pictures, shapes, charts and linked relationships.
Native Word DOC, DOCX and RTF with vector/SVG/SmartArt-like diagram content and AlternateContent.
Native Word DOT, DOTX and converted DOCX glossary fixtures; exact AutoText/glossary inspection is in glossary-inspection.json.
Native Word DOC, DOCX and RTF multilingual fixture with Arabic bidi, Japanese East Asian text, language/font declarations and markers; not yet merged into common manifest metadata.

environment_notes: Native Word provenance is Microsoft Office Word 16.110.2 build 16.110.26062818 on macOS for the finalized corpus where inspection metadata exists.
The corpus includes native Word DOC/DOCX/DOTX/DOT/RTF artifacts; bidi/east-Asia files are on disk but were intentionally not added to common metadata by this audit.
Current Word-for-Mac observations are bounded UI observations. They are not claims about Word on Windows, older Word releases, enterprise services, or every Office build.
Password, signature and trust rows remain external handoffs; no credentials, certificates or passwords are invented here.

high_value_missing_native_families.bounded_plan: Author a picture/table with Word Insert Caption and, if exposed, one AutoCaption rule; save DOC and DOCX, close/reopen natively, then inspect caption fields/sequence.

high_value_missing_native_families.family: Footnote-area columns and saved collapsed outline heading
high_value_missing_native_families.bounded_plan: Probe each feature in a small native DOCX and require the exact sectPr footnoteColumns or pPr collapsed element before marking evidence.
If Word exposes Master Document/Insert Subdocument, create one master plus one child and inspect link fields/relationships after reopen.
Use native Insert Symbol with a symbol likely to require the extension and inspect run XML; ordinary Unicode text is insufficient.

rows.rationale: The corpus has no deterministic current Word-for-Mac authoring route for Word 2003 XML schema-reference streams; the limitation is a bounded UI/workflow observation, not proof that no Windows/legacy route exists.
rows.next_action: Leave pending unless a controlled Office build can author an XSDR/TIQ document.

rows.feature: Structured document tags (`SttbfBkmkSdt`, SDT bookmark PLCs, `SDTI`)
rows.scope: Structured document tags (`SttbfBkmkSdt`, SDT bookmark PLCs, `SDTI`)
rows.rationale: Current Word-for-Mac Developer controls exposed legacy Text/Check/Combo form fields, not the legacy DOC SDT bookmark PLC authoring surface; absence is reported only for this observed UI route.
rows.next_action: Probe a Windows/older Word route only if SDT bookmark fixtures are required.

rows.rationale: Format-consistency checker marks are generated diagnostic state. No deterministic native Word authoring action was observed that records a stable fixture payload.
Text Services Framework UIM tables are editor/platform integration state; no deterministic native Office document authoring route was observed on the current Mac environment.

rows.feature: Grammar checker cookies (`Plcfcookie` and legacy cookies)
rows.scope: Grammar checker cookies (`Plcfcookie` and legacy cookies)
rows.rationale: Grammar-checker cookies are proofing-engine state. The current native workflow does not expose a deterministic command to author a stable cookie fixture.
Language auto-detection PLC state is proofing-engine metadata rather than a stable content feature; no deterministic native authoring route was observed.
Table-character cache records are derived caches. Current Word authoring creates tables but does not provide a controlled command for a chosen cache payload.
E-mail revision threading depends on mail integration and collaboration state; no deterministic local Word authoring route was observed.
Repair bookmarks are emitted by repair/recovery paths. No deterministic clean Word authoring action can create a chosen repair record.
Native Word annotation/bookmark evidence is present in the review-controls DOC; this verifies the bounded annotation-story/bookmark shape only, not every legacy annotation bookmark table.
VBA digital-signature storage needs a real certificate/signing identity. A macro-enabled Word fixture can be authored, but signing cannot be claimed without the external certificate handoff.
rows.next_action: Obtain a user-approved signing certificate and record the exact certificate/trust context before authoring.

rows.rationale: Saved selection is transient application/transaction state rather than stable authored document content; a fixture cannot truthfully prove the library operation semantics.
rows.next_action: Keep the matrix operation tests as the oracle; do not require a native fixture.

rows.rationale: Paragraph-group properties are internal layout/optimization state; current Word authoring provides no deterministic control over a chosen PGPArray/PGPInfo payload.
Native Word section/page setup evidence is present in the tables-layout DOC; this covers the authored section, orientation, margins and page-layout subset, not printer-driver specific records.
Native Word frame/list-shaped OfficeArt/VML content is present in the visual-objects and vector-diagram DOCs; this is bounded object/frame evidence and does not assert every Dofr variant.
MsoEnvelope metadata belongs to legacy envelope/mail integration. No current local Word authoring route was observed; this does not rule out an older Windows workflow.

rows.feature: Word 97+ FIB and versioned FibRgFcLcb tables
rows.scope: Word 97+ FIB and versioned FibRgFcLcb tables
rows.rationale: The native Word97 DOC corpus contains real FIB and versioned FibRgFcLcb tables, including text, tables, review and glossary DOC artifacts; this verifies the bounded native package baseline.
Native DOC fixtures carry Word document/summary properties and versioned DOP-backed metadata; the evidence is bounded to properties observable in these files.

rows.feature: WordDocument, table, Data, and story ranges
rows.scope: WordDocument, table, Data, and story ranges
rows.rationale: Native DOC fixtures exercise WordDocument/table/Data stories and story ranges through main text, notes, headers/footers, review and glossary content; no claim is made for every range combination.

The finalized native Word binary DOC corpus does not contain a custom XML data-store artifact, and no deterministic current Word-for-Mac route for authoring one in a DOC was observed. The cited DOCX customXml bibliography part is a separate package-format boundary and must not be promoted to DOC evidence.
rows.next_action: Only close with a native Word binary DOC that visibly and structurally preserves a custom XML store; keep DOCX customXml evidence separate.

rows.rationale: Native DOC summary/document-summary property streams are present in the authored DOC corpus; exact property values are fixture-specific and do not establish all versioned property fields.
Native text/review DOC and DOCX fixtures contain user-authored hyperlinks and relationship targets, which bounds the reserved user-link metadata surface; inert target resolution is not claimed.
Password-to-open encryption requires a human-supplied password handoff. The current encrypted candidate remains plaintext until that handoff is completed.
rows.next_action: Complete the password handoff, then save/reopen native encrypted DOC and DOCX variants.

rows.feature: XML signatures storage and signatures stream
rows.scope: XML signatures storage and signatures stream
rows.rationale: XML signatures require a real certificate and signing identity; a local native fixture cannot establish signature validity without that external trust context.
rows.next_action: Use a user-approved certificate handoff and preserve the signature/trust metadata separately.

rows.feature: Information Rights Management Data Space and protected content
rows.scope: Information Rights Management Data Space and protected content
rows.rationale: IRM/protected-content authoring requires rights-management services and account policy that are unavailable in the current local workflow; do not infer universal product absence.
Arbitrary unknown CFB streams/storages are not a user-authored Word feature with a deterministic native command; ordinary CFB preservation is covered elsewhere, not this exact generic boundary.

rows.feature: CP, PLC, STTB, SPRM/PRL, and property storage primitives
rows.scope: CP, PLC, STTB, SPRM/PRL, and property storage primitives
rows.rationale: Every native Word97 DOC artifact supplies real CP/PLC/STTB/SPRM/PRL property-storage structures through ordinary Word-authored stories; the fixture set does not enumerate every primitive variant.

rows.feature: Piece table, compressed/uncompressed Unicode text, FKPs, BTEs, and BinTable
rows.scope: Piece table, compressed/uncompressed Unicode text, FKPs, BTEs, and BinTable
rows.rationale: The native Word97 corpus contains piece-table Unicode/compressed text and FKP/BTE/BinTable structures; this is a bounded read-path baseline across ordinary authored DOCs.

rows.feature: Main, footnote, endnote, header, comment, textbox, and header-textbox parts
rows.scope: Main, footnote, endnote, header, comment, textbox, and header-textbox parts
rows.rationale: Native DOC fixtures visibly and structurally contain main, footnote/endnote, header/footer, comment and textbox stories across text, tables, review and visual-object documents; coverage is bounded to those authored stories.
Native review and math-navigation DOC fixtures contain named bookmarks and bookmark ranges used by fields/navigation; this does not claim every bookmark PLC encoding.

rows.feature: Field PLCs and non-Plcfld text-only fields
rows.scope: Field PLCs and non-Plcfld text-only fields
rows.rationale: Native review, math-navigation and mail-merge DOC fixtures contain fields and text-only field forms; the evidence is bounded to those field families and cached results.

rows.feature: Tables, nested tables, cell/row marks, merges, and TAP properties
rows.scope: Tables, nested tables, cell/row marks, merges, and TAP properties
rows.rationale: The native tables-layout DOC contains authored tables including nested/merged cells and row/cell properties; this is the exact bounded table cluster, not every TAP combination.

rows.feature: Character, paragraph, table, section, and picture SPRM families
rows.scope: Character, paragraph, table, section, and picture SPRM families
rows.rationale: Native text, tables-layout and visual-object DOCs exercise character/paragraph/table/section/picture formatting properties; the matrix family remains broader than these examples.

rows.feature: Stylesheet, list templates, list overrides, names, and numbering
rows.scope: Stylesheet, list templates, list overrides, names, and numbering
rows.rationale: Native text, tables-layout, math-navigation and glossary DOC/DOT fixtures contain styles, list templates/overrides and numbering; exact list/style combinations remain fixture-bounded.

rows.feature: Section layout, columns, borders, page/line numbering, and note placement
rows.scope: Section layout, columns, borders, page/line numbering, and note placement
rows.rationale: Native tables-layout DOC sections exercise layout, columns/borders, page and note placement; line numbering and every legacy section SPRM are not asserted from this cluster.

rows.feature: PLRSID, saved-by, associated strings, proofing, grammar, and spelling PLCs
rows.scope: PLRSID, saved-by, associated strings, proofing, grammar, and spelling PLCs
rows.rationale: Native DOC metadata/settings and Word-authored proofing state are present across the text, review and tables fixtures; this is bounded observable metadata and not a claim that every proofing PLC is populated.
Auto-summary records are a deprecated/internal Word feature. No stable current Word-for-Mac authoring control was observed.

No finalized Word corpus file contains an explicitly authored Caption/AutoCaption table. Word Insert Caption/AutoCaption is a concrete native authoring path worth a small picture/table-caption DOC and DOCX pair.
rows.next_action: Author one picture/table with Insert Caption plus an AutoCaption rule if the current Word UI exposes it.

rows.scope: Smart tags and factoids (Plcffactoid, property bags, and related STTBs)
rows.rationale: Smart-tag/factoid property bags depend on retired recognition/integration features; no deterministic current Word authoring route was observed.
No finalized fixture demonstrates a Word master document with a linked subdocument. This is a concrete Word document-management family, but it needs a bounded native probe before broad closure.
rows.next_action: If the current UI exposes Master Document/Insert Subdocument, author one master and one child document and record link behavior.

rows.feature: Revision marks, author tables, and property revisions
rows.scope: Revision marks, author tables, and property revisions
rows.rationale: Native review-controls DOC contains tracked insert/delete revisions, authors and revision properties; accept/reject execution is classified separately as an operation.

rows.feature: Document variables, attached-template and web-export metadata
rows.scope: Document variables, attached-template and web-export metadata
rows.rationale: Native glossary DOT/DOTX and converted DOC fixtures provide attached-template/document-variable-adjacent template evidence and native building-block storage; web-export and every variable variant are not claimed.

ActiveX/OCX control semantics are Windows/COM integration features; current Word-for-Mac did not expose a controlled authoring route. This is a platform-boundary observation, not a universal format claim.

rows.feature: Document statistics and DOP version metadata
rows.scope: Document statistics and DOP version metadata
rows.rationale: Native DOC files carry document statistics and DOP/version metadata observable through the Word97 package; exact statistic values are fixture-specific.
Native math-navigation DOC includes the authored legacy Equation.3/MathType-compatible object fallback alongside OMML; this bounds legacy object presence and does not claim full MTEF semantics.

rows.feature: Command bars, keymaps, menus, toolbars, and UI customizations
rows.scope: Command bars, keymaps, menus, toolbars, and UI customizations
rows.rationale: Command bars, keymaps, menus and toolbar customizations are application UI state rather than stable document content; no current Mac Word document-authoring route was observed.
Routing slips and route-slip protection require legacy workflow/integration services; no deterministic current local Word route was observed.

“Complete later-version Word binary behavior” is a broad library compatibility claim. The native DOC corpus supplies bounded Word97 stories, but no finite fixture can prove completeness across all later-version binary records.
rows.next_action: Use targeted native fixtures for individual records rather than closing this umbrella row.

rows.rationale: Native Transitional DOCX/DOTX is present, but a fresh Word-for-Mac UI probe did not expose a Strict Save As route. This is an observed local UI limitation; it does not claim Word on every platform cannot emit Strict.
rows.next_action: Leave Strict pending unless a controlled Office build provides a native Strict save route.

rows.rationale: Native Word DOCX fixtures contain mc:Ignorable and AlternateContent, including vector/diagram content; this verifies the observed MCE package subset only.

rows.feature: Main document, settings, styles, numbering, theme, font table, comments, notes, headers, footers, glossary, and properties parts
rows.scope: Main document, settings, styles, numbering, theme, font table, comments, notes, headers, footers, glossary, and properties parts
rows.rationale: The native Word corpus covers main/settings/styles/numbering/theme/fontTable/comments/notes/headers/footers/properties across text, tables, review, math and visual fixtures; glossary-inspection.json proves a real DOTX glossary part, while converted word-glossary.docx explicitly loses that glossary part.
Source-preserving transactions describe library mutation/round-trip behavior, not a stable native Word-authored feature; native fixtures can be inputs but cannot close this operation row.
rows.next_action: Retain dedicated library transaction tests for this row.

rows.rationale: Cross-story hyperlink batching is a library operation over multiple stories; native files show individual links but cannot prove the batch transaction semantics.
rows.next_action: Keep operation tests separate from fixture coverage.

rows.rationale: Source-backed secondary-story text is an API projection/transaction concern. Native headers, footers, notes and comments provide inputs but do not prove the projection algorithm.
rows.next_action: Keep source-backed story tests as the oracle.

rows.feature: Ordered paragraph and run content projection
rows.scope: Ordered paragraph and run content projection
rows.rationale: Ordered paragraph/run content projection is a library traversal contract. Native authored paragraphs/runs are useful inputs but cannot close the ordering operation row.
rows.next_action: Keep traversal tests independent of native fixture status.

rows.rationale: A deterministic corpus scan found no stylesWithEffects part, and the current Word-for-Mac UI exposed no controlled authoring route for that separate part. This does not prove the part is impossible on other Office builds.
Digital signatures require a real certificate/signing identity and trust context; native Word fixture creation is blocked on that external handoff.
rows.next_action: Obtain a user-approved certificate handoff before creating and reopening signed DOCX/DOCM variants.

rows.rationale: Password encryption requires a human-supplied password handoff. The current word-encrypted.docx candidate is plaintext and therefore does not verify encryption.
rows.next_action: Complete password handoff, then save/reopen a native encrypted DOCX.

rows.feature: Information Rights Management and protected content
rows.scope: Information Rights Management and protected content
rows.rationale: IRM/protected-content authoring requires rights-management services/account policy absent from the current local workflow; this is a bounded environment limitation.

Native visual/text/review/mail-merge DOCX fixtures contain hyperlinks, media and external relationship records; the evidence is bounded to those targets and does not assert successful external retrieval.

rows.scope: Settings extension elements (chartTrackingRefBased, docId, conflictMode, discardImageEditingData, defaultImageDpi)

rows.scope: Generic compatSetting records and compatibility mode

rows.scope: W14 conflict revision markup (conflictIns, conflictDel, and custom XML conflict ranges)
rows.rationale: A deterministic scan found no w14 conflictIns/conflictDel content, and no native Word command for authoring conflict markup was observed. This does not claim that other Office conflict workflows cannot emit it.
Native visual-objects DOCX contains w14:anchorId on authored drawing objects; this is direct bounded anchor evidence.

No w:calendar=umalqura element was found in the finalized corpus and no deterministic local Word UI route for selecting this specialized calendar extension was observed; do not infer universal product absence.

No finalized DOCX contains sectPr footnoteColumns. A focused native Word footnote-area columns probe is a concrete missing family if the current Word UI exposes it; do not claim the extension from ordinary footnotes alone.
rows.next_action: Probe one document with multiple footnote columns and inspect sectPr/footnote parts; otherwise retain as unavailable.

rows.rationale: No finalized DOCX contains pPr collapsed. A focused native outline-heading collapse fixture is a concrete missing family if Word exposes the saved collapsed state.
rows.next_action: Author one collapsed outline heading and reopen natively before classifying.

rows.rationale: Native math-navigation/text DOCX numbering parts contain w15:restartNumberingAfterBreak; this directly covers the observed extension element.
No finalized DOCX contains the run symEx extension. A focused native Insert Symbol fixture can test whether current Word emits this extension; ordinary Unicode symbols do not close the row.
rows.next_action: Probe a symbol requiring the Word symEx representation and inspect the run XML.

rows.rationale: No custom XML data-binding/storeItemChecksum authoring route was observed in current Word-for-Mac; the math-navigation custom XML part is an unbound bibliography store, so it cannot close this row.
No w14 formattingAllowed element was found and the current Word-for-Mac UI exposed no controlled authoring path for this Word 2024 extension; this is a version/UI boundary observation.
Native tables/math/review DOCX fixtures contain authored footnote/endnote/list numbering and note placement; this is bounded note/list evidence, not every extended number-format token.

The review-controls DOCX contains revisions, but accepting/rejecting revisions is an operation applied to a document state; no native fixture should be treated as proof that the library operation is correct.
rows.next_action: Use the review fixture as input and retain accept/reject operation tests.

rows.rationale: Native math-navigation DOCX/DOTX contains Word bibliography custom XML storage and relationships. The current fixture is an empty/default source store, so populated bibliography source records remain unverified.
Smart tags are retired/integration-dependent; no deterministic current Word-for-Mac authoring route was observed and no smart-tag part is in the corpus.

rows.scope: Custom XML data stores and content-control bindings
rows.rationale: Native math-navigation DOCX/DOTX contains customXml data-store parts and relationships, plus one core TOC SDT. No user payload binding/storeItemChecksum is claimed.
Streaming document authoring is a library I/O/transaction behavior, not a persistent Word feature that native Office can author as a fixture.
rows.next_action: Retain stream-oriented library tests.

rows.rationale: Validation and document statistics are library inspection operations. Native properties/statistics are useful inputs but cannot verify the library’s validation algorithm.
rows.next_action: Keep validation/statistics tests independent of fixture classification.

rows.rationale: Source-bound sanitization and external-hyperlink redaction are library transformations. Native hyperlink fixtures supply inputs, but no saved Word file can prove redaction semantics.
rows.next_action: Retain transformation tests as the oracle.

rows.rationale: No ink/inkML part is present and no deterministic local Word-for-Mac Ink authoring route was established. This is a bounded platform/workflow observation, not a universal absence claim.
MS-OWEXML custom-function payloads are specialized extension content; no current native Word authoring route was observed, so a synthetic fixture would be misleading.
Signature trust/certificate status requires an external certificate chain and trust context. It must remain separate from a future signed-package fixture.
rows.next_action: Use the same user-approved certificate handoff as docx-084 and record trust status.

rows.rationale: Generic unsupported-extension namespace content is a preservation/round-trip boundary, not one finite user-authored Word feature. Existing native extension parts are evidence inputs, not proof of arbitrary namespace behavior.
rows.next_action: Use targeted package fixtures for each extension family rather than closing the generic row.
